name: Register-PSSessionConfiguration - Fix Kerberos Double Hop
description: Creates a custom PSSession configuration that runs as a specific credential, enabling Kerberos double-hop - passing credentials through a remote session to access a third machine. Solves the problem where Enter-PSSession or Invoke-Command can reach host 2 but can't access host 3 because TGTs don't forward by default.
source: CPTS Module 13: Active Directory Enumeration & Attacks
notes:
=== THE KERBEROS DOUBLE-HOP PROBLEM ===
Kerberos TGTs are not forwarded across sessions by default:
  AttackHost → PSSession WS01 (hop 1 works - TGT presented to WS01)
  WS01 → try to access DC01 from INSIDE the session (hop 2 FAILS)
  Why: WS01 got a service ticket for WinRM, but your TGT wasn't forwarded.
       WS01 has no TGT to present to DC01.

Symptom: 'Access denied' or 'no logon servers' when accessing network resources
from inside a remote PS session.

=== FIX: Register-PSSessionConfiguration ===
# ON THE INTERMEDIATE HOST (WS01), run as admin:
Register-PSSessionConfiguration -Name MyConfig -RunAsCredential INLANEFREIGHT\forend -Force

# Then restart WinRM:
Restart-Service WinRM

# From attacker host:
Enter-PSSession -ComputerName WS01 -Credential $cred -ConfigurationName MyConfig

# Now INSIDE the session, credentials are available for hop 2:
ls \\DC01\C$  → works now
Invoke-Command -ComputerName DC01 -ScriptBlock { whoami }  → works

=== WHY THIS WORKS ===
The custom configuration tells WinRM: 'When a session connects using MyConfig,
run AS the RunAsCredential account.' This loads a fresh logon session for
INLANEFREIGHT\forend on WS01, including a usable TGT that can be forwarded.

=== ALTERNATIVE APPROACHES ===
1. CredSSP (unsafe in prod - stores creds in LSASS of remote host)
2. Explicit -Credential in every command inside session (more noise)
3. Rubeus request TGT on remote host + inject → inject and use
4. PTH or PtT inside the remote session manually

=== CLEANUP ===
Unregister-PSSessionConfiguration -Name MyConfig
This removes the config to avoid leaving artifacts on the intermediate host.

defense.why_it_works: Register-PSSessionConfiguration creates a WinRM endpoint that runs under a specified RunAsCredential. When a remote session connects to this named configuration, WinRM starts a new logon session for the RunAsCredential account on the intermediate host - including a full Kerberos TGT. Subsequent commands in that session can present this TGT for third-hop authentication, bypassing the default Kerberos double-hop limitation (which prevents TGT forwarding across remoting hops).
defense.prerequisites: Local admin on the intermediate host (to register a PSSession configuration). WinRM enabled on intermediate host. Valid credentials for the RunAsCredential account. Attacker access to the intermediate host via an existing remote session.
defense.impact: Enables credential forwarding through multi-hop PowerShell sessions - allows reaching a third host (e.g., DC) from inside a session on an intermediate host. Embedded credentials in the endpoint configuration persist until explicitly unregistered, creating a standing backdoor for credential reuse.
defense.detection: Windows Security Event 4104 (Script Block Logging) for Register-PSSessionConfiguration if PowerShell logging is enabled. New PSSession configuration appearing in WSMan:\localhost\Plugin (visible via Get-PSSessionConfiguration). Event 400/800 in PowerShell operational log when sessions use the new endpoint. Event 4624 type 3 for the RunAsCredential account logging on when sessions connect. Monitoring Get-PSSessionConfiguration output for non-standard endpoint names.
defense.prevention: Restrict who can register PSSession configurations (requires local admin - enforce this via LAPS and tiered admin). Monitor WSMan:\localhost\Plugin for unexpected configurations. Disable WinRM on hosts that don't require remote management. JEA (Just Enough Administration) provides constrained endpoints that limit what commands can run - use instead of full RunAs configurations. Clean up (Unregister-PSSessionConfiguration) any non-default configurations as part of hardening.
defense.evasion: Give the configuration a name matching a legitimate-sounding administrative endpoint (e.g., 'ITAdmin', 'BackupService'). Use Unregister-PSSessionConfiguration immediately after the double-hop operation completes to remove the artifact. The RunAsCredential account's logon events on the intermediate host appear as normal network logons - no special indicator for 'RunAs via WinRM config'.
defense.misconfiguration: WinRM (Windows Remote Management) is enabled on servers and workstations, and domain admin credentials are used directly on remote hosts - placing their NTLM hash/TGT in LSASS on those machines. Enter-PSSession and evil-winrm both use WinRM to open remote PowerShell sessions. Privileged credentials touching non-Tier-0 machines is the core 'double hop' and credential exposure problem.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# WinRM enabled and listening on all interfaces:
Get-WSManInstance -ResourceURI winrm/config/listener -SelectorSet @{Transport='HTTP'}
# Address: *  (all interfaces - not restricted to management VLAN)

# Domain admin used directly on workstations (credential exposure):
Enter-PSSession -ComputerName workstation01 -Credential domain\Administrator
# Administrator hash/TGT now in LSASS on workstation01
# If workstation01 is compromised, admin credentials are extracted
defense.secure_config:
# Restrict WinRM listener to management subnet:
New-WSManInstance winrm/config/listener \
    -SelectorSet @{Transport='HTTP'; Address='10.10.1.0/24'}

# Tier 0 admin accounts NEVER log into Tier 1/2 machines:
# Privileged Access Workstations (PAW) model
# Domain Admins only RDP/PSSession to DCs from dedicated PAW machines

# Use JEA (Just Enough Administration) for delegated tasks:
# Constrained runspaces that only allow specific commands
New-PSSessionConfigurationFile -Path admin.pssc -SessionType RestrictedRemoteServer
Register-PSSessionConfiguration -Path admin.pssc -Name 'HelpDesk'

# Monitor: Event 4624 (logon type 3) for Domain Admins on non-DC machines
# Alert on admin credentials used on workstations

index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=3
| where AuthenticationPackageName="Kerberos" AND Account_Name!="*$"
| table _time, Account_Name, Source_Network_Address, Logon_Process

index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-WinRM/Operational" EventCode=91
| table _time, Computer, User, Message

event.code:"4624" AND winlog.event_data.LogonType:"3" AND winlog.event_data.AuthenticationPackageName:Kerberos

event.provider:"Microsoft-Windows-WinRM" AND event.code:"91"
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceEvents
| where ActionType == "PowerShellCommand"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "Register-PSSessionConfiguration"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, ProcessCommandLine
| union (SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4624 and LogonType == 3 | project Timestamp=TimeGenerated, DeviceName=Computer, InitiatingProcessAccountName=TargetUserName, ProcessCommandLine=IpAddress)
| sort by Timestamp desc

explain:
Creates a PSSession endpoint that runs as a stored credential, solving the Kerberos double-hop:
  Register-PSSessionConfiguration   define a custom WinRM endpoint
  -Name <sessname>         the endpoint name to connect to
  -RunAsCredential <domain>\<user>   run every session under these creds, so they exist on the box for a second hop
  -Force                   overwrite/skip prompts
Connect to it (Enter-PSSession -ConfigurationName <sessname>) and onward access to a third machine now authenticates, instead of failing with no forwarded credentials.
